projects.name: Improved access to bread through bread subsidy project
projects.description: Bread is a central component of the Syrian diet, accounting for around one third of daily caloric intake, yet worsening food insecurity affecting over 9 million people and shortfalls in national wheat production have made affordable bread increasingly difficult to access, with recent subsidy reductions driving sharp price increases and deepening hardship among vulnerable families. In response, WFP, in partnership with the Government of Syria through the Ministry of Economy and Industry, launched the Subsidized Bread Programme in 2025 to stabilize access, reduce household economic pressure, and support national food security by supplying WFP provided wheat flour to selected bakeries, enabling 2 million people in the most food insecure areas to purchase fortified bread at a fixed subsidized price that covers only operational costs while safeguarding access to a daily staple.

projects.name: Support diversified and sustainable livelihoods and food systems at household, community and national level.
projects.description: The project focuses on rehabilitating and improving irrigation systems and communal agricultural assets to enable smallholder farmers to resume cultivation, increase productivity, and revive local markets. In parallel, it restores and strengthens the bread value chain as a strategic pillar for sustainable, nutrition-sensitive access to food. By improving the availability and quality of bread, the project supports job creation and local economic recovery. Interventions span the full value chain, from direct support to farmers to the rehabilitation of silos, mills, and bakeries, alongside technical assistance and capacity strengthening to advance a national wheat flour fortification policy.

projects.name: EU Support for Safe Returns and a Stable Future for Syrian Returnees.
projects.description: With financial support from the European Union, this programme supports the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable reintegration of returning Syrian refugees, while strengthening national capacities to manage return and recovery and to support access to decent work. The programme is implemented jointly the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and ILO, in cooperation with national authorities, linking humanitarian assistance with early recovery and employment support. In Syria, the programme helps address legal and administrative barriers that affect returnees’ access to civil documentation, services, and employment. It provides reintegration support for returning families, including financial assistance and housing and shelter support for the most vulnerable, enabling returnees to meet immediate needs and start rebuilding their lives. The programme promotes livelihoods through skills development, developing public work schemes, job matching, and support to local employment initiatives aligned with local economic priorities, contributing to community stabilisation and social cohesion. It also strengthens coordination and information systems that support return and reintegration, including cooperation with neighbouring countries where relevant.

projects.name: Data for action, insight and foresight
projects.description:
IOM will support inter-agency data collection efforts through the roll out of its Displacement Tracking Matrix for Syria. Data will be gathered through a network of field-based enumerators and shared with other donors and humanitarian agencies to help inform the response. IOM will:
Establish broad coverage of mobility tracking data collection exercises through baseline area and location assessments to determine presence of IDPs, returnees and affected populations and identify critical gaps in services, displacement triggers and priority humanitarian needs;
Strengthen early-warning systems through triggering Onset Displacement Tracking upon sudden large-scale movements of IDPs or returnees observed in any area of Syria to provide actionable locational level information on an evolving displacement/return situation; and
Undertake Area of Return Monitoring to gather information on the situation in areas of return, focusing on key pillars, namely security, livelihood and infrastructure, access to services and priority needs, and social cohesion, and enable IOM and partners to assess the severity of living conditions in areas of return and provide key data on the conditions faced by returnees.

projects.description:
IOM plays a global role in supporting post-conflict societies and governments in designing and implementing comprehensive Transitional Justice (TJ) frameworks, focusing on safeguarding Housing Land and Property (HLP) rights and ensuring victims' access to reparations. Based on IOM’s work to safeguard the HLP rights of Syrian households since 2021, the proposed interventions will integrate multidisciplinary solutions to address HLP restitution, compensation, psychosocial rehabilitation, and other reparative mechanisms tailored to local needs. IOM will:
Conduct baseline assessments, engaging communities, developing tailored frameworks, documenting and safeguarding HLP claims securely;
Design efficient claim processing systems; and
Build the capacity of local actors, including the provision of policy guidance, expert advice, and technical assistance for civil, mental health and psychosocial support assistance, legal assistance, and HLP rights, and to implement reparations and manage grievances effectively guided by psychosocial considerations.

projects.name: The Nexus Response Mechanism (NRM) in Syria
projects.description: The Nexus Response Mechanism (NRM) aims to strengthen the humanitarian-development-peace nexus in Syria by addressing immediate needs while building long-term resilience among conflict-affected populations, including displaced persons, host communities, and returnees. The NRM focuses on reducing vulnerabilities through capacity development, preparedness for future shocks, and promoting human rights-based approaches. By linking relief efforts with early recovery and sustainable development, the NRM facilitates transitions from emergency assistance to durable solutions, particularly in protracted displacement settings and areas affected by inter-communal violence. Special emphasis is placed on empowering women and the most vulnerable while ensuring interventions align with due diligence criteria to foster security, stability, and resilience in conflict-affected regions.

or mobility needs. To strengthen community-based protection, UNRWA will expand Area Protection Committees and 
engage volunteers in awareness-raising activities.

projects.name: Provide nutrition assistance to prevent chronic and acute malnutrition
projects.description:
Under this activity, WFP implements a supplementary feeding programme to prevent malnutrition among children aged 6 to 23 months from eligible households receiving general food assistance, through the distribution of medium quantity lipid based nutrient supplements. In collaboration with UNICEF, the programme integrates counselling on infant and young child feeding and promotes improved complementary feeding practices, including guidance on dietary diversity and age appropriate food quantities. In targeted locations, pregnant and lactating women and girls who are enrolled in general food assistance also receive cash based transfers to support improved dietary diversity and nutrition outcomes.
